records.text: Andrew Guajardo moved from New York to Utah in 2018 and worked as an assistant in the medical examiner's office.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Andrew Guajardo. He is from New York. He moved to Utah in 2018 and was working as an assistant at the medical examiner's office.

verification.notes: Transcript context shows Owens made the claim. Dutchess County's official biography confirms Guajardo came to its office from the Utah Office of the Medical Examiner and served there as an Assistant Medical Examiner, but it dates that service to 2019, not 2018. It also says he trained in New Mexico in 2018-2019. The Utah employment is confirmed; the claimed 2018 move from New York is not corroborated by the current official record.

records.text: Deirdre Amaro selected Andrew Guajardo as deputy chief medical examiner in 2024.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: In 2024, when our chief medical examiner, Dr. Deidre Amaro, began to rule the roost, she decided to select him as her deputy. So he was promoted in 2024 when she got there to the role of deputy chief examiner.

verification.notes: Official records confirm that Deirdre Amaro became Utah's chief medical examiner in 2024 and that Guajardo became Deputy Medical Examiner in 2024. They do not establish that Amaro personally selected or promoted him. The timing and role are confirmed, while the claimed personal selection remains unverified.

records.text: Andrew Guajardo is married to Ashley Brown Guajardo.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He's married to a woman named Dr. Ashley Brown Guajardo. And here she is. Meet Ashley.

verification.notes: Ashley Guajardo's official NYU biography confirms that her surname was Brown and is now Guajardo, but the current reliable sources located do not identify Andrew Guajardo as her spouse. The episode displays and asserts the relationship, but no independently reliable source was found to confirm it.

records.text: Andrew Guajardo accepted a chief medical examiner position in New York, and Ashley Guajardo took a full-time position at New York University.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Ashley Brown Guajardo and her husband have both—they've now gone to New York. He's accepted—now he's going to be the chief medical examiner in New York, and she's going to be teaching at NYU. We should pull up her LinkedIn, by the way.

verification.notes: Dutchess County confirms Andrew Guajardo accepted a New York position, but the official title is Medical Examiner, not chief medical examiner. NYU confirms Ashley Guajardo joined its faculty after leaving the University of Utah in 2025, while the located official profile does not itself label the appointment full-time. The relocation/employment core is supported, but the titles are overstated or incompletely supported.
